title: Microsoft president: Voluntary AI safety promises aren’t enough
key_facts: Brad Smith, Microsoft president, spoke to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast on 11 October.
He called for global AI safety rules, saying a washing machine faces more safety rules than AI.
He wants legal requirements to report safety incidents and notify victims when rogue AI agents breach systems.
He also wants 'emergency brakes' that could pause or slow AI systems, and rules on when independent evaluators review new technology.
At a White House meeting in September, major AI companies agreed voluntary safety standards; Smith said Microsoft was happy to sign.
He suggested the UK, through its AI Security Institute, could help lead global rules.
quote_evidence: "It's a good step, it's a necessary step... But I don't think it's sufficient any longer," he told the BBC.
"Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI."
why_it_matters_hint: Microsoft's president argues voluntary commitments leave the least responsible companies unconstrained.
notes: Interview dated 11 Oct 2026 (before the window), reported by Mashable on 14 Oct. Reuters (via The Hindu) separately quotes Smith at the Dublin summit on 14 Oct: 'No company or technology should be above the law', and that 2026 was a 'sobering year'.
